blocks.label: dotagent
blocks.title: One repo configures every coding agent on a machine
blocks.summary: dotagent keeps shared guidance, skills, hooks and settings in one checkout and links them into each agent's config directory. A single install script runs one installer per tool.

blocks.label: install
blocks.title: install runs one installer per tool
blocks.summary: The top-level script parses its flags, then runs install-claude, install-herdr and install-tuicr in that order.

blocks.label: install-pi
blocks.title: Pi is configured last, with optional flags
blocks.summary: install forwards --pi-dir and --provider to install-pi only when they are given. Without them install-pi runs with its defaults. Passing --provider without --pi-dir is a usage error.

blocks.label: install-claude
blocks.title: install-claude links files into ~/.claude
blocks.summary: It creates the target directories, links the shared files, then installs plugins through the claude CLI.
steps: Create the skills, agents, hooks and commands directories
Link AGENTS.md as CLAUDE.md, then link or copy settings.json
Link the statusline and the implementer agent
Hand the skills folder to install-skills
Install plugins with the claude CLI

blocks.label: install-skills
blocks.title: Each skill folder is symlinked, never overwritten
blocks.summary: For every folder in skills/ it creates a symlink in the target directory. It skips a link that is already correct and stops on anything else.
blocks.code:
for skill in "$SOURCE_DIR"/*/; do
  name="$(basename "$skill")"
  target="$TARGET_DIR/$name"

  if [[ -L "$target" ]]; then
    current="$(readlink "$target")"
    if [[ "$current" == "$skill" ]]; then
      continue
    fi

    echo "Refusing to replace symlink: $target -> $current" >&2
    echo "Expected: $skill" >&2
    exit 1
  fi

  if [[ -e "$target" ]]; then
    echo "Refusing to replace existing path: $target" >&2
    exit 1
  fi

  ln -s "$skill" "$target"
done

blocks.label: settings
blocks.title: Settings are linked, or copied on a read-only checkout
blocks.summary: Claude Code rewrites settings.json when plugins or marketplaces change. If the checkout is not writable, such as a read-only mount, the script copies the file instead of linking it.
blocks.code:
# Claude Code rewrites settings.json when plugins or marketplaces change, so a
# read-only checkout (an ADE workbench mount) gets a copy instead of a link.
if [[ -w "$DOTFILES" ]]; then
  ln -sf "$DOTFILES/claude.settings.json" "$CLAUDE/settings.json"
else
  rm -f "$CLAUDE/settings.json"
  install -m 644 "$DOTFILES/claude.settings.json" "$CLAUDE/settings.json"
fi

blocks.label: hooks and commands
blocks.title: Hooks and commands are linked one file at a time
blocks.summary: Every file in hooks/ is linked into ~/.claude/hooks, and every commands/*.md into ~/.claude/commands. The commands loop skips the glob when nothing matches.
blocks.code:
for hook in "$DOTFILES/hooks"/*; do
  ln -sf "$hook" "$CLAUDE/hooks/$(basename "$hook")"
done

"$DOTFILES/install-skills" "$DOTFILES/skills" "$CLAUDE/skills"

for command in "$DOTFILES/commands"/*.md; do
  [[ -e "$command" ]] || continue
  ln -sf "$command" "$CLAUDE/commands/$(basename "$command")"
done

blocks.label: plugins
blocks.title: Plugins come from the claude CLI
blocks.summary: The superpowers uninstall and the marketplace adds may fail without stopping the script, because of || true. The two plugin installs may not.
blocks.code:
echo "Installing Claude plugins..."
claude plugins uninstall superpowers@superpowers-dev --scope user --keep-data || true
# A fresh install knows only the built-in directory, not this marketplace.
claude plugins marketplace add anthropics/claude-plugins-official || true
claude plugins install frontend-design@claude-plugins-official --scope user
claude plugins marketplace add hegeldev/hegel-skill || true
claude plugins install hegel-skill@hegeldev --scope user

blocks.label: conflict rule
blocks.title: An existing path is a conflict, not something to replace
blocks.summary: A symlink that already points at the right folder is skipped. A symlink to anything else, or a real file or directory at the target, stops the script with exit 1. Re-running is safe, and a conflict is loud.
